note: All puzzles were picked from the full bank (not retired) and their answers were checked visually against the figures. Do not change answers. Option images are option_<LETTER>.png; angle ranking and cube counting have text options.

puzzles.question: Which opening could the object pass through?
puzzles.rule_line: The object can't rotate once it starts through. Only one opening fits.
puzzles.why_it_fits: A is the object's outline seen straight on along one of its main directions: the low step and the tall block line up exactly.

traps.B: The outline of a different side, changed so it can't pass.
traps.C: An L-shape that doesn't match any of the object's outlines.
traps.D: The same L-shape as C, just smaller. Size changes don't make it fit.
traps.E: The same L-shape again, at a third size. None of them match.

puzzles.question: Which drawing is the missing TOP view?
puzzles.rule_line: Solid lines = visible edges. Dashed lines = hidden edges.
puzzles.why_it_fits: B shows the curved cut corner and the hole exactly where the front and end views put them.

traps.A: Draws an extra edge across the object that doesn't exist.
traps.C: Missing the curved cut. The object is built differently.
traps.D: Right features, but the hole is in the wrong place.

puzzles.question: Rank the four angles from SMALLEST to LARGEST.
puzzles.rule_line: Ignore line length. Only the opening between the lines counts.
puzzles.why_it_fits: 4 is narrowest (about 38 deg), then 3 (about 42 deg), then 1 (about 47 deg), and 2 is widest (about 52 deg).

traps.B: Swaps 3 and 4, the two closest angles. Long arms on 4 make it look bigger.
traps.C: Swaps 1 and 2, the two widest angles.
traps.D: The right idea, but ranked largest to smallest. Read the question twice.

puzzles.question: The paper is folded, then punched through all layers. Which is the unfolded pattern?
puzzles.rule_line: Unfold in reverse order. Every hole mirrors across each fold it went through.
puzzles.why_it_fits: Undo the 3 folds in reverse. The hole mirrors across each fold it was folded over, giving 5 holes.

traps.A: A hole is shifted by one grid cell.
traps.B: Too few holes: a stacked layer of paper was ignored.
traps.D: Too few holes: a stacked layer of paper was ignored.
traps.E: Has a hole that no layer of paper produces.

puzzles.question: How many cubes have exactly 4 painted faces?
puzzles.rule_line: The whole figure is painted on every exposed side except the bottom.
puzzles.why_it_fits: Count only cubes with exactly 4 painted faces (the bottom is never painted, and faces touching another cube are not painted). There are 4.

traps.A: 1 is the count for exactly 5 painted faces, a different question.

puzzles.note: Question changed from 5 to 4 painted faces by the owner on 24 Oct 2026; answer (4 cubes = D) supplied by the owner. a012.png still shows the old answer and is not used.

puzzles.question: Which solid does the pattern fold into?
puzzles.rule_line: Track where the dark triangle and the half-dark face end up after folding.
puzzles.why_it_fits: C is the only option with both shaded areas exactly where the pattern puts them once it's folded.

traps.A: The shading is on the wrong face.
traps.B: The shading is on the wrong face.
traps.D: The shading is on the wrong face.

puzzles.question: SUNDAY CHALLENGE: Which solid does the pattern fold into?
puzzles.rule_line: All four look alike. Compare proportions, not just shape.
puzzles.why_it_fits: C is the only option whose proportions match the pattern's faces.

traps.A: The right kind of solid, but its proportions are off.
traps.B: The right kind of solid, but its proportions are off.
traps.D: This pattern can't fold into it: a face has the wrong shape.
